meta.description: Machine-readable vocabulary that separates target-repository agent surfaces, SAGE maintainer surfaces, target scopes, and validation corpus evidence.

actor_surfaces.label: Target Repository Coding Agent
actor_surfaces.purpose: Use SAGE evidence to edit the analyzed repository with the smallest safe patch.
must_not_receive: SAGE platform release/debug posture by default
external corpus calibration logs by default
raw output/.raw artifact paths as edit instructions
actor_surfaces.path_contract: Open files with analysis_root plus target_file, target_files, related_files, inspect_first, or listed file/path fields.

actor_surfaces.label: SAGE Maintainer Agent
actor_surfaces.purpose: Develop or debug SAGE itself, including release proof, capability registry, and internal provenance.
must_not_receive: permission to mutate customer target repositories without an explicit target-repository packet
actor_surfaces.path_contract: Use SAGE workspace paths and SAGE maintainer documentation; do not conflate these with target-repository edit paths.

system_scopes.subject: SAGE product source, release, development governance and internal evidence
must_not_include: customer runtime findings as SAGE debt unless they prove a product defect or generalized lesson

system_scopes.subject: The analyzed customer or internal target repository
Reusable platform contracts whose implementation serves both realities with scoped evidence
must_not_include: an unscoped verdict or authority transfer between SAGE and a target repository

system_scope.meaning: Whose engineering reality, authority, debt, lessons and proof are being evaluated.

acquisition_mode.meaning: How the repository root is selected; this must not redefine repository semantics.

authority_rules.public_source_development_rule: Public users may inspect, modify and test the SAGE source under the applicable license through target-repository profiles. This does not publish or grant private SAGE maintainer governance, institutional memory, release-proof, seal or publication authority.

parity_invariants: Default and explicit target repository modes use the same topology producer.
Default and explicit target repository modes use the same engine semantics, applicability rules and claim boundaries.
Acquisition mode may change artifact namespace, cache lifecycle, permissions and target-root routing only.
A default repository result and explicit target result for the same root, snapshot, config projection, project scope and pipeline profile must be semantically equivalent.
forbidden_inferences: absence of target_root alone determines SAGE_ON_SAGE
external acquisition defines a second repository ontology
folder names or source markers grant SAGE_ON_SAGE authority
analyzing SAGE source as a repository inherits private lessons debt roadmap release proof or seal authority

target_repository.runtime_finding_source: target-repository work queue, watchdog pulse ledger, quality gates and target proof artifacts

target_scopes.label: SAGE Self Target
target_scopes.description: The SAGE product source analyzed explicitly through the shared external-target isolation path for maintainer surgery.
target_scopes.artifact_scope: output/external_targets/<sage_source_slug> with a separate SAGE_ON_SAGE proof subject
target_scopes.agent_usage: SAGE maintainer agents only. Resolve through config/reality_target_profiles.json; never infer this scope for a target-repository agent.

target_scopes.label: Internal Target Repository
target_scopes.description: The analyzed repository tree adjacent to or containing SAGE; in this workspace it can include MAIN plus variations and companion projects.
target_scopes.agent_usage: Target-repository coding agent may use these packets when analysis_root points at the analyzed repository root.

target_scopes.label: External Target Repository
target_scopes.description: A repository analyzed from outside its tree through target_root and isolated output/external_targets artifacts.
target_scopes.agent_usage: Target-repository coding agent may use these packets when analysis_root points at the external target root.

target_scopes.label: Corpus Validation Pool
target_scopes.description: Representative external repositories and fixtures used to calibrate and prove SAGE behavior-family coverage.
target_scopes.artifact_scope: corpus docs, fixtures, validation reports, and output/external_targets evidence
target_scopes.agent_usage: SAGE maintainer agents may use this evidence for product hardening; it must not be injected into normal target-repository coding packets by default.

surface_rules.rule: Default target-repository packets must prefer operation directives over SAGE platform status, debug provenance, release posture, or corpus calibration history.

Default coding packets for internal target repositories are MAIN/host-first. Variation and companion projects may be shown only for explicit merge, diff, proof, corpus, or all-project inspection tasks.
External target packets must read isolated artifacts for the requested target_root and fail closed when required artifacts are missing.
Corpus evidence may support SAGE release claims and regression tests, but it is not ordinary coding context for a customer target repository.
SAGE self-analysis must be requested explicitly as a target scope; it must not be inferred from ordinary MAIN or external target packets.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Self-map and source-layer inventory identify the SAGE workspace and product layers.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Discovery and project registry identify MAIN, variations, companions and isolated external targets.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Never infer SAGE self-target scope from an ordinary customer target root.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: SAGE self-map, source-layer inventory and Python/JavaScript source inspection describe the product codebase.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Atlas, Genome, Fractal Map and source snapshots describe the analyzed repository.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Reuse canonical analyzers; do not copy a second self-analysis engine or mix customer artifacts with SAGE self artifacts.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Seal impact, git/mtime evidence and release freshness detect protected SAGE changes.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: SQLite source_snapshots, hashes and watchdog freshness detect target source drift.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: A source hash match is not a human seal; SAGE release seal and target doctrine/patch authority remain separate.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Self-map revalidation scopes and connectivity map describe likely product impact.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Blast radius, upstream trace, test impact and dependency health provide surgical change impact.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Self-target impact augments release-proof ownership; it does not replace SAGE contract and release validators.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Self-development constitution, governance registry, release claims and central decision contracts constrain SAGE changes.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Project doctrine, policy, principle packs, cages and Architecture Oracle proposals constrain target changes.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: SAGE product doctrine cannot silently govern a customer repository, and customer doctrine cannot change SAGE release claims.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Developer skill and self-map guide maintainers, but no explicit self-target surgical packet workflow is active.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: ContextOS, inspect tools and surgical operation packets provide bounded source-grounded context.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: The maintainer projection may expose SAGE internals; the target-repository projection must not.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: The development loop requires targeted validation and release-proof refresh but is not driven by a dedicated self-target watchdog session.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Watchdog refreshes changed truth, preserves unread findings and records deep-proof debt.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Self watchdog remains advisory and must not recursively trigger full release proof or mutate SAGE without human approval.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Targeted validators, unit tests and release slices validate SAGE patches.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: validate_patch, get_test_impact and command contracts validate bounded target patches.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: A clean patch check does not satisfy SAGE release proof or customer runtime proof.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: System health, release readiness, final suspicion and claim guard evaluate SAGE product readiness.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Audit, quality gates, confidence, ecosystem readiness and merge readiness evaluate the target repository.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Neither health surface may be presented as the other subject's verdict.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Release proof bundle proves only the scoped SAGE product release claim.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Underlying proof artifacts exist, but one target repository proof envelope is roadmap work.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Target proof must state its own claim boundary and cannot inherit PASS from SAGE release proof.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Audit lesson registry converts product-development findings into guards, debt or roadmap evidence.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: A read-only target lesson projection preserves recurrence candidates and explicitly target-bound human confirmations without reading SAGE product lessons.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Customer lessons belong to that target and must enter SAGE product memory only when they prove a generalized product defect or reusable lesson.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Central work-item registry preserves deferred SAGE product debt.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Violation queues, proof debt and merge queues preserve target actions, but they are not SAGE product debt.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Do not copy runtime target findings into the SAGE work-item registry unless they identify a SAGE defect or generalized platform debt.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Capability and roadmap registries govern product evolution and release claims.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: A customer repository may have product plans, but SAGE does not replace its issue tracker or roadmap source of record.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Future adapters may bind ADR/issue/roadmap evidence without making SAGE the customer's planning system.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: System spine and connectivity map connect layers, steps, artifacts, validators and proof surfaces.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Atlas graphs and target lineage connect source truth, findings, packets and validation flow.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Do not merge the SAGE product nervous-system graph with a customer's repository dependency graph.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Layered checklist, progress ledger and release micro-walkthrough audit SAGE itself.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Agent packet manual evidence and corpus/fixture reviews sample target behavior, but no customer-wide clone of the SAGE self-audit is needed.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Use representative source-grounded target review; do not expose SAGE internal layer audit or release micro-step noise to target agents.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Hardcoded decision inventory and central decision validators guard SAGE configuration drift.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Project-calibrated magic literal and config hygiene cage is roadmap work.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Target literals require doctrine/policy calibration; SAGE internal centralization rules cannot become universal blocking rules.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Claim guard and final consistency align product docs, capabilities and release identity.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Code-to-README/API/ADR freshness is roadmap work.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Documentation evidence must remain scoped and cannot prove runtime behavior by text alone.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Step timings, heartbeats, performance budgets and release telemetry describe SAGE execution.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Watchdog timings and proof debt exist, while normalized local governance outcome telemetry is roadmap work.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Local-first, opt-in telemetry must separate SAGE runtime performance from customer repository engineering outcomes.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: No general SAGE self-development equivalent is required unless SAGE itself adopts explicit variation projects.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Variation review, merge waves, simulations and human-gated MAIN candidates are active target capabilities.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Do not preload variation evidence into normal MAIN editing or SAGE maintainer context.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Maintainers use external targets and corpus evidence to calibrate SAGE behavior.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Customers may analyze independently located repositories through isolated external-target artifacts.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Corpus calibration evidence is never ordinary customer coding context.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Clean mirror, installation smoke and distribution cleanup prove SAGE packaging.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Not a target-repository governance responsibility.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Never run SAGE distribution cleanup against a customer repository or active SAGE source workspace.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Plugin manifests, contribution trust and extension contracts govern SAGE evolution.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Target repositories may expose their own extension boundaries, but SAGE V1 does not install or execute third-party target plugins.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Do not execute untrusted extension code before sandbox, permission and revocation contracts exist.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Release validators and manual audits exist, but controlled SAGE-on/off outcome evals are roadmap work.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: Agent correction outcomes can supply future local private-eval evidence.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: Do not claim causal agent improvement before fixed-task controlled evaluations exist.

bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_sage: Human-controlled multi-agent development occurs operationally, but explicit coordination contracts are not active.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.sage_on_repository: MCP and deterministic artifacts are multi-agent compatible, not a lock/ownership coordinator.
bidirectional_capability_transfer_matrix.boundary: SQLite compatibility and shared packets do not prove safe concurrent multi-agent writes.
